Method and data

How the forecast is made, and what happens to your data.

The same method sits behind the free Delivery Scan and the Delivery Audit. It is a standard method, and it fits on this page. This is the page to send to whoever has to approve the connection.

From your tracker to a chance

01

How your team really finishes work

Not the plan and not the estimates. The dates on which items actually moved and got done, fast weeks and slow weeks included.

02

What is left

Every open item behind the date, including what was quietly added after you agreed on the scope.

03

Played forward 10,000 times

Each run draws from your team's real weeks and plays the remaining work forward. Some runs finish early, some late. The share that finishes by your date is your chance.

Figure: 10,000 runs become one curve

What it captures, and what it can't

It captures

The full range of speeds your team has actually had. The weeks reviews dragged, someone was out, a dependency didn't land. The patterns your team already lives with.

It can't

Predict what has never happened. If your lead architect leaves next Tuesday, no model saw that coming. That's rarely what catches teams, though. It's the slow build-up of ordinary weeks.

The chance is the best case. It assumes the work stays as it is today and your team keeps its recent pace. Most teams add work along the way. Then the real date is later than the number says. The calculation is the easy part. Holding the date is the work.

The realistic date is the date that 85 of 100 runs finished by. It is not a promise: 15 finished later.

For a roadmap, the Delivery Audit never counts your team twice. The work behind each deadline is forecast in the order you plan to build it, on top of what comes before. It does not simulate dependencies between items. Where one thing waits on another, I read that in the data and report it in words.

Why not a dashboard?

Tools like ActionableAgile, LinearB or Jellyfish are good at what they do: they show an engineering team how its work moves. They tell you where you are.

The forecast tells you where you're going to end up, for a date you've already promised to someone.
